title: Noor and the Cipher
premise: When the coffin of Ashford Vale's founder, Edmund Fairweather, is exhumed for a heritage project and found empty, insurance investigator Rafael Fairweather — a distant relation with a photographic memory — recognizes a cipher in the founder's ledger that he has seen before in five years of claims files. With archivist Noor Haddad, who catalogued the town's records and knows which pages were quietly removed, Rafael decodes a ledger of payments and favors revealing that the town's founding families have been extorting each other for generations, and that Edmund faked his own death to escape them. As the founding families close ranks, burn archives, and frame Rafael for theft, the two uncover that Edmund's body was never found because he died trying to expose the ledger — and his killer still sits on the town council. In the climax at the flooded quarry vault where the original ledger is hidden, Rafael trades his perfect memory of the town's secrets for Noor's life, then publishes everything anyway, choosing truth over belonging.
about_author: Petra Blackwood is a former forensic accountant who spent a decade untangling small-town financial frauds before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the arithmetic of secrets from a farmhouse full of rescued greyhounds.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He attends the exhumation as the insurer on the heritage grant, photographing every detail out of habit. When the coffin lid lifts on nothing but settled dirt, the mayor's smile flickers half a second too long. The beat: unease disguised as professionalism — Rafael notices everything and admits nothing.

chapters.title: Five Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Establishing his gift: he recalls every claim file verbatim, including the ones he was told to lose. A flashback to being ordered to bury a fire report introduces the town's quiet economy of favors. Beat: loneliness of a man who remembers what everyone else agrees to forget.

chapters.title: Noor of the Stacks
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The town archivist, an outsider like Rafael, discovers three folios missing from the founder's collection — cut cleanly, catalogued as never existing. She brings it to Rafael because he's the only person who ever read the whole archive. Beat: cautious kinship between two people paid to keep secrets.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Studying the surviving ledger, his memory flags repeating marginal marks matching notation from old insurance claims — a bookkeeping cipher. Someone has been reading this ledger for decades and leaving it in the open precisely because no one looks. Beat: the thrill of the first real thread.

chapters.title: The Founder's Funeral That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Digging into 1962 records, she finds contradictions: no death certificate filed locally, a closed-casket service, and a gravedigger's log with an impossible entry time. Edmund Fairweather may never have been buried at all. Beat: dread blooming under curiosity.

chapters.title: Council of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He interviews the four founding-family heirs on the council, memorizing their tells. Councilwoman Vesper Thorne warns him off with velvet courtesy; old Aldous Pike slips him a key 'by mistake.' Beat: the reader feels the walls of a closed system closing.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She reconstructs the 1987 archive fire from Rafael's remembered claim file, proving it was set to destroy one specific box. The arson claim was denied — by Rafael's own predecessor, who retired rich. Beat: anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Numbers That Name People
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Decoding the first cipher entries: sums mapped to initials reveal blackmail payments flowing between founding families for sixty years — and a final column of payments to someone designated only 'E.F., alive.' Beat: vertigo; the mystery stops being historical.

chapters.title: The Man Who Remembers Too Much
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Rafael's office is ransacked; nothing stolen except his annotated ledger copy. Police chief Dane Merrick — a founding-family son-in-law — suggests Rafael himself staged it. Beat: fear arriving not as violence but as implication.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Following the ledger's oldest reference, they find the disused quarry and a submerged pump house. Diving isn't possible yet, but Rafael photographs tool marks proving recent visits. Someone else knows. Beat: the race formally begins.

chapters.title: Vesper's Version
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Vesper Thorne invites Noor to tea and offers her Rafael's job — and Rafael's ruin — if she walks away. Vesper frames it as mercy: 'Edmund tried to save this town from itself. Look how that ended.' Beat: temptation wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: E.F., Alive
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Cross-referencing pension ledgers, Rafael finds E.F.'s payments ended abruptly in 1994 — the year a vagrant drowned in the quarry. He realizes Edmund lived hidden for thirty years and died violently. Beat: grief for a man he never met, and fury at whoever kept the secret.

chapters.title: The Gravedigger's Daughter
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They track down the gravedigger's daughter, now elderly, who confesses her father buried a weighted coffin and helped Edmund disappear — until someone made him stop talking. Her father's suicide note was typed. Beat: the human cost surfaces; stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: Frame Job
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael is arrested for stealing archival property; the planted evidence is flawless, built from details only someone with access could know. In holding, he recites his alibi from memory so precisely it unnerves Chief Merrick. Beat: the hero cornered by his own gift turned against him.

chapters.title: Noor Breaks the Code Alone
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. With Rafael jailed, Noor cracks the cipher's final layer using his dictated notes: the ledger's true index points to a map keyed to church hymn numbers. She must decide whether to trust Aldous Pike, who keeps appearing wherever she turns. Beat: courage without backup.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Confession
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Aldous visits the jail and confesses he was Edmund's courier — and that he reported Edmund's hiding place to the others in 1994, believing they'd only buy his silence. His guilt bought Rafael's release: he names Merrick as the one who went to the quarry that night. Beat: complicity revealed; no villain is simple.

chapters.title: Hymns at Midnight
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following the hymn-number map through the church crypt, Noor finds the route to the quarry vault — and realizes she's been followed. She hides the decoded page inside a hymnal and runs. Beat: terror and ingenuity in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Freed, Rafael reaches the pump house as Merrick arrives to destroy the vault. In the dark, Rafael's memory becomes a weapon: he narrates Merrick's own movements back to him from prior nights of surveillance photos, unraveling him. Beat: the climax ignites — mind against muscle.

chapters.title: Drowning Truth
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Merrick takes Noor hostage at the water's edge, demanding the ledger. Rafael offers the trade — his complete testimony, every secret he holds, erased in exchange for her. Merrick hesitates; Vesper arrives and orders Merrick to stand down, choosing the town's survival over its lie. Beat: sacrifice offered, power's logic exposed.

chapters.title: Edmund's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They open the vault: Edmund's skeleton, his final journal, and the master ledger. His last entry names his killer — Merrick's father — and forgives the town anyway. Noor reads it aloud to the assembled founders. Beat: catharsis; the dead finally permitted to speak.

chapters.title: Everything I Remember
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the public inquiry, Rafael testifies for eleven hours from pure memory, dismantling sixty years of denials. Vesper resigns rather than face him; Merrick is charged. The town turns on Rafael for the destruction even as it thanks him. Beat: victory with a bitter aftertaste — truth costs belonging.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Record
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating. Months later, Noor reopens the archive with an honest catalogue, and Rafael, no longer the town's filing cabinet, accepts a teaching post — and her invitation to stay. The last line: some things are worth remembering out loud. Beat: belonging chosen freely, identity rebuilt on truth.
